message.text: `runCheck` measures and trims the check's local findings against `SightingBudget.checkRecord`. The bound exists to keep the exported check record under `recordLimit`. For every `static.*` check, though, `ReviewRecords.check` → `sorted` → `sighting` replaces each sighting's message, What, Why here and What to do with fixed text ("`<check>` reports `<rule>` here. withheld." / `withheld`). So the exported bytes do not depend on the text the budget measures and trims at all. Trimming a static check's findings cannot shrink its exported record, and the budget cannot tell whether that record will fit. There is a second gap. Biome's and tsc's Why here is a short fixed sentence (`${tool} reports this at head but not at the base…`, about 77 bytes), shorter than every note (108 bytes or more). So `#cut`'s `shrinks` is false for all of them: they are never abridged, only passed whole or refused.

## Known limits

The budget measures a check's findings as the check forms its outcome, not the records the review exports. [Issue #626](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/626) would measure those instead. Until it lands, three cases remain, chosen by the coordinator on 2026-11-20 on [issue #605](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/605). None lets a verdict pass that should block, since the verdict is decided from the local findings, which are complete:

- **The relay batch.** Each check's record fits the store alone, but the relay carries a round's records in one batch of at most 8 MiB. Three valid 3 MiB check records pass the store and the verdict, and the relay then refuses the batch. The reader sees a refused relay, and the round's records are lost.
- **A projection smaller than the local findings.** The shared record replaces a static tool's text with fixed sentences. A check whose own text is long can fail as too large when its projected record would fit. The reader sees a failed check, and the review reads not reviewed.
- **A projection larger than the local findings.** For Biome and tsc, the projected fixed sentences are longer than the local text: 518 bytes against 487 for one finding's message and explanation. A static check whose local findings come within about 6% of the limit can pass the budget while its exported record is past it. The store then refuses the record after the verdict is stored. The reader sees a store error with exit code 2, and no verdict in CI.

- `ReviewRecords` rewrites every static finding a record holds, in a check's or a lens's sightings and a dismissal's, Biome and tsc included. Core's `staticFindings` gives those two a fixed sentence now, but a build from before [issue #281](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/281) stored their text, and the check's name says nothing of which build wrote a sighting. Melian's round two found the first form, which left Biome and tsc alone by their check's name, trusting a label. Any static check, one Melian adds later included, is rewritten: the rule denies by default.
- A rewritten finding's message and `explanation.what` read "`<check>` reports `<rule>` here.", then the fixed sentence `withheld`. Its `whyHere` and `whatToDo` are `withheld`. It keeps its rule, place, snippet, trigger and ID, which are the head's own content. Core's `Finding.parse` takes the ID from path, rule, snippet and discriminator, never from the message, so the rewritten finding still parses with its ID.

explanation.whatToDo: Measure what is exported. Build the projected sightings (`sorted(sightings)`, i.e. `shareable(sighting(f))`) and fit those against the budget, or have `runCheck` measure each finding by its projected size. Only trim local findings whose projection gets smaller. Otherwise move the fit to where `ReviewRecords.check` forms the record, and fail the check there before adjudication stores a verdict.
explanation.whyHere: The change exists so that a store refusal no longer follows a stored verdict of findings (issue #605). It extends the budget to "every check's record", and design.md says "Biome, tsc, Enola or mutation findings past it are trimmed alike". For static checks the bound measures the wrong thing, so the failure it was added to prevent still happens. It also fails closed on records that would fit, and it strips local detail that brings no saving at export. The decision file lists these cases as known limits until #626, and a documented gap does not excuse the bound.

properties.failureScenario:
Case 1, Biome/tsc, store error after a verdict. A head adds about 9,000 `debugger;` lines under ordinary paths. `static.biome` writes about 4.18 MB of local sightings, under the budget of 4,190,208 bytes. `fit` returns them unchanged (sighting-budget.ts line 60), the check reads `ran`, and adjudication stores a verdict of findings. At export, `sighting()` rewrites each Biome finding to the fixed sentences, which run longer than the local text (518 against 487 bytes, by the decision's own count). The check record passes 4,194,304 bytes, `storable()` throws `invalidRecord`, and the review exits with a store error (code 2) with the verdict standing. That is issue #605's failure, now for Biome. Trimming could not help even a little past the budget: the export does not use the trimmed text, and Biome findings never count as shrinking.

Case 2, Enola/mutation, refused when it would fit. A change gives `static.enola` or `static.mutation` many findings whose tool-written messages are long, for example mutant replacements. `fit` keeps the tool-written headline as What and still passes the budget, so it throws `recordTooLarge` and the review reads not reviewed. The exported record would replace all that text with `withheld` and fit easily. Below that point, the same check gets its local detail (terminal and local store) trimmed with no saving in the shared record.
